title: Comparison of the effectiveness of in-person versus online physiotherapy after a joint intensive week in a spa resort on the risk of falls - A randomized controlled study
summary: In the study setting of the randomized controlled pilot study, both groups start with a shared week at the health resort. At the beginning of the week, the groups are randomized and divided into two study arms. During the intensive week, interventions for each group already take place. After the intensive week, the study arm OTAGO-plus will go through a new program that takes place online at home and is designed in accordance with the fall prevention strength training OTAGO from New Zealand (Campbell et al. 2023). The study arm AHAB-plus is the control group and visits the therapy center once a week, undergoing the fall prevention program according to the specifications of the licensing provider AHAB (approved by the Central Prevention Testing Center, ZPP, under § 20 SGB V; this paragraph of the Fifth German Social Code regulates preventive services and the legal requirements under which statutory health insurance funds can cover preventive measures, currently 80 euros per measure).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Eligible participants are those who meet all of the following criteria:
1) The person is between the ages of 50 and 80.
2) The person is able to walk independently.
3) The person lives within a 60-km radius or a 1-hour drive from Hopfen am See.
4) At least one of the following statements applies:
a) The person has fallen in the past year.
b) The person feels unsteady when walking or standing.
c) The person is concerned about falling.
5) The person is cognitively capable of and willing to use a computer.
Exclusion criteria:
Prospective participants who meet at least one of the following criteria will be excluded:
1) The person has undergone surgery on the lower extremities within the past 12 months (e.g., hip replacement, knee replacement, femoral neck fracture, ankle surgery, vascular surgery, etc.)
2) The person is cognitively unable to perform the required tests and exercises.
3) The person has been diagnosed with overt osteoporosis.
4) The person is currently pregnant.
5) The person has an underlying visual or neurological condition that is incompatible with the exercises.
